title: REACT3D: Real-time Edge Accelerator for Incremental Training in 3D Gaussian Splatting based SLAM Systems
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) SLAM requires incremental training and rendering at over 30 FPS on edge devices, but existing GPU-based solutions and prior accelerators fall short due to redundant training computation, unnecessary loss computation, and irregular memory access patterns. The combination of continuous camera streaming, per-Gaussian gradient accumulation, and sparse activated Gaussian sets creates severe compute and memory irregularity.
motivation: Real-time 3DGS-SLAM on edge platforms is a critical capability for autonomous robots and AR/VR systems, and no prior hardware design achieves the 30 FPS real-time threshold required for accurate tracking and mapping.
method: REACT3D introduces two algorithmic optimizations: (1) spatial consistency and convergence-aware sparsification that predicts under-optimized Gaussians based on spatial coherence and convergence dynamics, eliminating redundant forward/backward rendering passes; and (2) a pixel block-wise fine-grained dataflow that fuses loss computation into the rendering pipeline, removing explicit loss storage. At the architectural level, a Content Addressable Memory (CAM)-based Dual-index Gaussian Buffer resolves discontinuous memory accesses by maintaining two parallel indices into the Gaussian buffer, avoiding computation conflicts during gradient merging across scattered Gaussian-to-pixel mappings.
key_novelty: The CAM-based Dual-index Gaussian Buffer that resolves the irregular memory access and gradient-merging conflict problem inherent to 3DGS training on sparse, streaming SLAM data.
contributions: Spatial consistency and convergence-aware sparsification algorithm that eliminates redundant Gaussian forward/backward passes
Pixel block-wise fine-grained dataflow that fuses loss computation and eliminates explicit loss memory traffic
CAM-based Dual-index Gaussian Buffer microarchitecture for irregular memory disambiguation during gradient merging
First hardware design demonstrated to meet real-time (>30 FPS) requirements for 3DGS SLAM on an edge device, achieving 12.10x speedup and 33.69x energy efficiency over NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 33.69x energy efficiency improvement over NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin

limitations: Evaluation is limited to the 3DGS SLAM domain; generalizability of the CAM-based buffer and sparsification to other NeRF variants or volumetric representations is not discussed.
